title: Realization of a simplexwise trivial Kan fibration
statement: Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, horns and realization of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the category $\mathcal K$ of k-spaces of [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits]. Let $q:E\to B$ lift against every horn inclusion $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$. Suppose that for every simplex $b:\Delta^n\to B$ there are a simplicial set $F_b$ and an isomorphism $\Delta^n\times_BE\cong\Delta^n\times F_b$ over $\Delta^n$. Then for every $m\geq0$ and continuous maps $a:D^m\to|E|$ and $h:D^m\times[0,1]\to|B|$ with $|q|a(z)=h(z,0)$, there is a continuous $\widetilde h:D^m\times[0,1]\to|E|$ with $\widetilde h(z,0)=a(z)$ and $|q|\widetilde h=h$. Here $D^m$ is the closed Euclidean unit ball, $D^0$ is a point, and products are in $\mathcal K$. Neither $E$ nor $B$ is required to be Kan; the fibres can be empty.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.1 and its proof, printed pp. 95–97 Read online; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial-homotopy theorem.

proof.text: First replace the disk parameter by a cube, without changing the lifting problem. For $m>0$, the map from $[-1,1]^m$ to $D^m$ sending $x\ne0$ to $x\|x\|_\infty/\|x\|_2$ and $0$ to $0$ is a homeomorphism: its inverse sends $y\ne0$ to $y\|y\|_2/\|y\|_\infty$. The two formulas are inverse by homogeneity of the norms; continuity at zero follows from $\|x\|_\infty\le\|x\|_2\le\sqrt m\|x\|_\infty$. Rescaling gives $\theta:[0,1]^m\cong D^m$; for $m=0$ use the identity of a point. Write $P=[0,1]^{m+1}$, with last coordinate time, $g(x,t)=h(\theta(x),t)$ and initial map $a\theta$. This cube is compact Hausdorff. Indeed, the simplex whose coordinates $w_v$ are indexed by its $2^{m+1}$ vertices is compact by [lem-coef-standard-simplex-compact], and $w\mapsto\sum_vw_vv$ is a continuous surjection onto $P$: at $x\in P$ take $w_v=\prod_{v_j=1}x_j\prod_{v_j=0}(1-x_j)$. These weights sum to one and have barycenter $x$. An open cover of the image pulls back to one of the compact simplex, proving compactness. Distinct points are separated by a differing real coordinate.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.1, first paragraph; explicit cubical parameter and compactness calculation replacing the disk parameter.

proof.text: Apply [lem-cbc-realization-compact-finite-support] to the compact Hausdorff cube $P$ and $g$. Obtain a finite simplicial subset $A\subseteq B$ and a continuous $g_A:P\to|A|$ factoring $g$. Put $E_A=A\times_BE$. The pullback comparison of [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] identifies $|E_A|$ with $|A|\times_{|B|}^{\mathcal K}|E|$. Consequently $(g_A(x,0),a\theta(x))$ is a continuous initial lift into $|E_A|$. Every simplex $b:\Delta^n\to A$ has $\Delta^n\times_AE_A=\Delta^n\times_BE$, so the given product isomorphisms remain available. Horn lifting is inherited too: compose a lifting square with $A\to B$, lift in $E$, and pair with the specified map to $A$. It suffices to solve the problem over $A$, then compose the lift with $|E_A|\to|E|$.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.1, printed pp.95–96: finite-base reduction and the realized pullback square.

proof.text: We prove by induction on the number of nondegenerate simplices of a finite simplicial set $A$ that every map $E_A\to A$ trivial over each simplex has local product charts after realization, with products in $\mathcal K$. A local product chart means an open subset $U\subseteq|A|$, a k-space $T$, and an isomorphism $U\times^{\mathcal K}T\cong U\times_{|A|}^{\mathcal K}|E_A|$ over $U$; restrictions are k-ified subspaces. For the empty base this is vacuous. Choose a nondegenerate simplex $b$ of maximal dimension $n$ and remove it and its degeneracies, leaving $Z\subset A$. The unique nondegenerate decomposition in [lem-cbc-realization-cw-subcomplex] shows that $Z$ is a simplicial subset, every proper face of $b$ belongs to $Z$, and $A=Z\amalg_{\partial\Delta^n}\Delta^n$. Degree by degree, the pushout adjoins precisely the degeneracies of the one missing nondegenerate simplex. Pulling this pushout back along $E_A\to A$ gives $E_A=E_Z\amalg_{\partial\Delta^n\times_AE_A}(\Delta^n\times_AE_A)$: its degreewise elements over $Z$ are already in $E_Z$, and all other elements occur in the adjoined summand, with exactly the boundary identifications. Realization preserves these pushouts, and identifies all their pullbacks and products, by [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits]. Thus with $S=|\Delta^n|$, $\partial S=|\partial\Delta^n|$, and $f:\partial S\to|Z|$, the base is the topological attachment $|A|=|Z|\amalg_fS$, and the total space is the corresponding attachment of $|E_Z|$ and $S\times^{\mathcal K}|F_b|$. The subspace and characteristic-map assertions in [lem-cbc-realization-cw-subcomplex] identify the boundary and the open simplex interior in these descriptions.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.1, printed p.96: induction on nondegenerate simplices and its displayed boundary-attachment square; degreewise justification supplied.

proof.text: If $n=0$, the attachment is a disjoint new vertex, with total space its product with $|F_b|$, so it supplies a chart and preserves the old ones. Suppose $n>0$. The simplex product isomorphism gives a chart $\psi:S\times^{\mathcal K}F\cong S\times_{|A|}^{\mathcal K}|E_A|$, where $F=|F_b|$. It supplies charts over all points of the new simplex interior, an open subset of $|A|$. For a point of $|Z|$, the induction hypothesis supplies an open neighborhood $U\subseteq|Z|$ and a chart $\phi:U\times^{\mathcal K}T\cong U\times_{|A|}^{\mathcal K}|E_A|$. Put $U'=f^{-1}(U)\subseteq\partial S$, and let $\phi'$ be its pullback chart. If $U'=\varnothing$, $U$ is already open in the attachment and its chart is enough. It remains to extend this chart when $U'\ne\varnothing$.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.1, printed p.96: simplex chart, old-base chart and the case of empty boundary preimage.

proof.text: Here is the required collar, including the correction of the source's introductory retraction sentence. In barycentric coordinates $t_0,\ldots,t_n$ on $S$, put $\mu(t)=\min_jt_j$. Away from the barycenter set $r_j(t)=(t_j-\mu(t))/(1-(n+1)\mu(t))$. These continuous nonnegative coordinates sum to one and one is zero, so $r:S\setminus\{\text{barycenter}\}\to\partial S$ is continuous and is the identity on $\partial S$. Choose $0<\epsilon<1/(n+1)$ and take $V=\{t:\mu(t)<\epsilon,\ r(t)\in U'\}$. It is open in $S$, $V\cap\partial S=U'$, and $r:V\to U'$ is a retraction. The subset $W=U\amalg_{U'}V$ of the attachment is open: its inverse images in the two quotient summands are precisely $U$ and $V$. It contains the chosen old-base point. The boundary is not asserted to retract from the whole simplex; only this open collar is used.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.1, printed p.96: open thickening of the boundary preimage; explicit barycentric collar formula repairs the preceding informal sentence.

proof.text: On $U'$ compare the two charts without making a choice of a homeomorphism between their fibres. Write $\psi^{-1}\phi'(u,t)=(u,\alpha(u,t))$ and $(\phi')^{-1}\psi(u,s)=(u,\beta(u,s))$, with $t\in T$, $s\in F$. The second coordinates are continuous and satisfy $\beta(u,\alpha(u,t))=t$ and $\alpha(u,\beta(u,s))=s$. The maps $C(v,t)=(v,\alpha(r(v),t))$ from $V\times^{\mathcal K}T$ to $V\times^{\mathcal K}F$ and $C^{-1}(v,s)=(v,\beta(r(v),s))$ are continuous inverse maps over $V$. Define $\rho=\psi C$. Since $r|_{U'}$ is the identity, $\rho|_{U'}=\phi'$. These equations remain valid if the fibres are empty; no point of either fibre is selected.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.1, printed pp.96–97: the transition maps and extension along the collar retraction; the two possibly different fibre spaces are kept explicit.

proof.text: Glue $\phi$ and $\rho$ to obtain a product chart over $W$. We justify continuity of both the glued map and its inverse, rather than treating compatible pointwise charts as enough. The exponential law in [lem-coef-kspace-exponential-law] makes $(-)\times^{\mathcal K}T$ a left adjoint: maps out of $L\times^{\mathcal K}T$ correspond to maps from $L$ into the specified mapping k-space. The colimit universal property then shows that this product preserves the pushout $W=U\amalg_{U'}V$. By step 3, the total space over $W$ is the pushout of the restrictions over $U$ and $V$ along their common boundary restriction; restricting a topological quotient to the inverse image of an open subset is a quotient, since that inverse image is saturated and open. These statements also hold with the k-ifications specifying the restrictions. Explicitly, a continuous map from a k-space $L$ to a space $H$ is continuous into $kH$: for every k-open subset $O$ of $H$ and every compact test $c:C\to L$, the set $(fc)^{-1}O$ is open, so $f^{-1}O$ is open by the defining test condition on $L$. The converse follows from the continuous identity $kH\to H$. This verifies the required mapping universal properties after k-ification. The maps $\phi$ and $\rho$ agree on the boundary restriction by step 6, as do their inverse maps. Therefore the two pushout universal properties glue them to continuous inverse maps $W\times^{\mathcal K}T\cong W\times_{|A|}^{\mathcal K}|E_A|$. This covers every old-base point. Together with step 4 it proves the induction claim for $A$, hence local product charts for every finite base, without assuming the base or total simplicial set is Kan.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.1, printed p.97: gluing the modified chart; continuity expanded using the k-space exponential law instead of an uncited product/quotient assertion.

proof.text: Apply these charts to $g_A:P\to|A|$ and pull their open domains back to an open cover of the ordinary metric cube $P$. The following compactness argument produces a grid fine enough for that cover. For each $x\in P$ choose $r_x>0$ so that the relative ball of radius $2r_x$ about $x$ lies in one chosen cover member. Finitely many relative balls of radii $r_x$ cover $P$ by the compactness proved in step 1. Let $\delta>0$ be the minimum of their radii. For any subset $Q\subseteq P$ of diameter $<\delta$, choose $y\in Q$ and a selected ball containing it; the triangle inequality puts all of $Q$ in the corresponding ball of radius $2r_x$, and hence in one chart domain. Choose an integer $N$ with $\sqrt{m+1}/N<\delta$; the closed boxes of the regular $N$-by-$\cdots$-by-$N$ cubical grid therefore each map under $g_A$ into one chart. No general theorem about Hurewicz fibrations or fibre bundles is used here.

source.place: Agent expansion of the local-product-to-disk-lifting reduction in Proposition 3.6.1, printed p.96; direct finite-subcover argument in place of the cited Spanier theorem.

proof.text: Order the grid boxes first by increasing time interval and then lexicographically by their $m$ spatial interval indices. Start with the prescribed lift on $P_0=[0,1]^m\times\{0\}$. Suppose a lift has been constructed on $P_0$ and all earlier boxes and let $Q$ be the next box. Its intersection $A_Q$ with that old domain is its bottom time face together with its lower spatial face in each direction whose interval index is positive. Indeed each such adjacent lower box is earlier. Any earlier box meeting $Q$ either is in an earlier time layer and meets its bottom, or has a first differing smaller spatial index and meets a lower spatial face there. This also accounts for all intersections of higher codimension. In normalized coordinates $u_1,\ldots,u_{m+1}\in[0,1]$ on $Q$, let $J$ consist of the time coordinate and precisely these positive-index spatial directions. Then $A_Q=\{u:\min_{j\in J}u_j=0\}$. The explicit retraction $R_Q:Q\to A_Q$ subtracts $\lambda=\min_{j\in J}u_j$ from coordinates in $J$ and leaves all other coordinates unchanged. It is continuous, remains in the cube, reaches $A_Q$, and fixes $A_Q$. The set $J$ is always nonempty, including $m=0$.

source.place: Agent cubical proof of the local-product lifting step in Proposition 3.6.1; explicit attaching order and retraction.

proof.text: Choose the chart containing $g_A(Q)$. Express the old lift on $A_Q$ in this chart as $(g_A(u),s(u))$, where $s:A_Q\to T$ is its continuous fibre coordinate. Extend over $Q$ by the formula $u\mapsto\phi(g_A(u),s(R_Q(u)))$. It lies over $g_A(u)$ and restricts to the old lift because $R_Q$ fixes $A_Q$. The chart and its inverse are maps in $\mathcal K$; the maps from $Q$ and $A_Q$ into their k-ified restrictions are continuous as well: these domains are compact Hausdorff (finite unions of closed faces of a compact cube), so they are themselves among the compact tests defining k-ification. Thus the displayed formula defines an ordinary continuous map on $Q$. Glue it to the old lift. This is continuous: for a closed subset of the target, the inverse images on the finitely many closed boxes and the bottom face are closed there, hence closed in their finite union. Induction through the finite list constructs a continuous lift on $P$ with exactly the prescribed bottom value. If a chart fibre is empty, the already prescribed lift on the nonempty bottom face of the box would supply a point of it; thus such a box cannot arise in a lifting problem that has the prescribed initial map. No global nonemptiness hypothesis has been inserted.

source.place: Agent cubical proof of the local-product lifting step in Proposition 3.6.1; extension formula, finite closed pasting and empty-fibre check.

proof.text: Compose this lift into $|E_A|$ with $|E_A|\to|E|$ as in step 2 and precompose its spatial parameter with $\theta^{-1}$. The resulting map $\widetilde h:D^m\times[0,1]\to|E|$ is continuous. At time zero its value is $a(z)$ because the construction never changed the prescribed initial map; its projection is $h(z,t)$ because each box formula projects to $g_A$ and $|A|\to|B|$ carries $g_A$ to $g$. This proves both required equalities for every $m\geq0$. Neither the finite reduction, the collar induction nor the cubical lift required any nonempty fibre or any Kan condition on $E$ or $B$.

source.place: Proposition 3.6.1, conclusion; return from the finite-base pullback and cubical parameter.

lean.statement: theorem realization_of_simplexwise_trivial_kan_fibration (E B : SSet.{u}) (q : E ⟶ B) (hq : ∀ (n : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ i : Fin (n + 1), HasLiftingProperty (SSet.horn n i).ι q) (htriv : ∀ (n : ℕ) (b : SSet.stdSimplex.obj ⦋n⦌ ⟶ B), ∃ (F : SSet.{u}) (e : pullback b q ≅ SSet.stdSimplex.obj ⦋n⦌ ⊗ F), e.hom ≫ CartesianMonoidalCategory.fst _ _ = pullback.fst b q) : ∀ (m : ℕ) (a : C(TopCat.disk.{u} m, SSet.toTop.obj E)) (h : C(TopCat.disk.{u} m × unitInterval, SSet.toTop.obj B)), (SSet.toTop.map q).hom.comp a = h.comp (ContinuousMap.prodMk (ContinuousMap.id _) (ContinuousMap.const _ 0)) → ∃ (ht : C(TopCat.disk.{u} m × unitInterval, SSet.toTop.obj E)), ht.comp (ContinuousMap.prodMk (ContinuousMap.id _) (ContinuousMap.const _ 0)) = a ∧ (SSet.toTop.map q).hom.comp ht = h
lean.note: Direct continuous-map formulation of disk lifting. The dependency identifies SSet.toTop with the underlying k-space realization; the closed Euclidean disk and its cylinder already have their k-space topologies. No new notion or auxiliary theorem is required.
